references.text: [ref:Prov 20:18|Proverbs 20:18] emphasizes that plans should be made with wise counsel and war conducted with good strategy—the same principle of carefully assessing the situation before acting that Jesus teaches in the parable.

[ref:Prov 24:6|Proverbs 24:6] states that through wise leadership one can wage war, and victory comes with many advisors. This reflects Jesus' point about carefully considering one's resources before going to war.

In [ref:1 Kgs 20:11|1 Kings 20:11], the king of Israel warns against boasting before the battle is decided. The principle is the same: one should carefully evaluate the outcome before committing oneself.

The preceding parable about the tower builder in [ref:Lk 14:28-30|Luke 14:28-30] carries the same message: one must calculate the cost beforehand. Both parables serve as illustrations of what it takes to be a disciple of Jesus.

[ref:Lk 14:33|Luke 14:33] gives the conclusion for both parables: whoever does not give up all that they own cannot be a disciple of Jesus. The parable about the king considering war points forward to this requirement of total surrender.

In [ref:2 Kgs 18:19-25|2 Kings 18:19-25], the Assyrian king confronts Hezekiah with the question of whom he trusts when rebelling—a practical illustration of having to assess one's resources against a superior enemy.

In [ref:2 Chr 25:17-24|2 Chronicles 25:17-24], Amaziah ignores Joash's warning and goes to war without carefully assessing the situation, leading to disaster. This illustrates the consequences of not following the principle Jesus describes.
